What was wrong or missing in v1.0: The January and February to March examples named E1038 and E1046 — a third-party helper and a contractual daily-wage worker, neither of whom is leave eligible and neither of whom could carry a proration credit.
What v1.1 does about it: Examples corrected. E1069 added as a leave-eligible January joiner, and a leave-eligibility check column added so the same mistake is visible next time.

What was wrong or missing in v1.0: Sheet 19 held six comp-off credits; the ledger carried three of them, none of the consumptions and not the lapse. A balance built from the ledger disagreed with the comp-off register for four of five workers.
What v1.1 does about it: Five movements added and the two sheets reconciled. 53_Leave_Balance_AsOn is derived from the ledger alone.

What was wrong or missing in v1.0: LL-0029 was a two-day casual leave debit whose own narration said no leave was applied and LOP was raised instead — two days silently removed from a balance.
What v1.1 does about it: Changed to a zero-day no-movement row so the rejected application stays visible without touching the balance.

What was wrong or missing in v1.0: GL-009 and GL-010 debit the gratuity and leave-encashment provisions with no credit account anywhere in the map, so any journal containing them was short by 700,000 and could not balance. LE-02 had no professional tax credit account at all.
What v1.1 does about it: Four mappings added: GL-024, GL-025, GL-026 and GL-027.

What was wrong or missing in v1.0: E1021 Rekha Deshpande is named in the demo script as the grade-exempt case for demo point 12 and had no punches and no attendance, so half of that point could not be shown.
What v1.1 does about it: 26 punch events and 15 attendance days added — five lates beyond grace in one month, every day still Present.

What was wrong or missing in v1.0: The record carried 21 columns and none of the attributes the WIP requirements are about: rest-day applicability, OT eligibility basis, leave scheme, COFF lapse, payroll versus attendance location, continuous service or gate-pass entitlement.
What v1.1 does about it: 22 policy columns added, every value derived from the category, designation and worker class masters so the resolution order can be shown rather than asserted.

What was wrong or missing in v1.0: A band letter but no numeric grade rank, so every "and above" rule had nothing to compare against and would have had to match a designation name.
What v1.1 does about it: Grade rank and default leave scheme added. AGM and above is rank 70; Assistant Manager and above is rank 50.

What was wrong or missing in v1.0: No roles, no users, no data scope anywhere in the dataset — demo point 8 is about who is signed in, and it could not be run at all.
What v1.1 does about it: 43_Roles_and_Data_Scope and 44_Demo_Users added, ten sign-ins each tied to a point in the script.

What was wrong or missing in v1.0: VN-01 to VN-05 were referenced on the employee record and in the contract-labour register but never defined.
Demo point 1 asks for the dinner break to be reported separately and there was no break-level data.
What v1.1 does about it: 49_Break_Register added, distinguishing punched breaks from the scheduled shift break.

What was wrong or missing in v1.0: Runs existed at header level only — no employee lines, no journal, no bank file — so demo points 10 and 15 could be described but not shown.
What v1.1 does about it: 55_Payroll_Register, 56_GL_Journal and 57_Bank_File added. Both journals balance and reconcile to the bank files.

What was wrong or missing in v1.0: The clearance checklist and the settlement run existed with nothing in between — no amounts.
What v1.1 does about it: 58_FnF_Settlement added for both cases, including the gratuity contrast at seven years against four.

What was wrong or missing in v1.0: Every location named a professional tax slab set and no slabs existed anywhere.
What v1.1 does about it: 48_PT_Slabs added for four states. Values are demo figures and must be confirmed against current notifications.

What was wrong or missing in v1.0: Requisitions pointed at candidates who did not exist; confirmation and pre-boarding had no records.
Employment categories, leave schemes, the combination matrix, the grace policy and the night extension rule were all stated as rules with no configuration behind them.
What v1.1 does about it: 38, 39, 40, 41 and 42 added. Every number the client stated as policy now sits in a row rather than in the engine.

What was wrong or missing in v1.0: The dataset could not seed a tenant on its own — the value sets lived only in the specification workbooks.
Nothing tied the dataset back to the specifications, so there was no way to tell what was missing.

Type: v1.1, September 2026. Four defects and thirteen gaps. The four defects matter more than the gaps: a missing sheet is visible while you prepare, but a leave ledger that does not reconcile to the comp-off register only shows up when a client asks you to explain a balance, and an unbalanced journal only shows up in front of a finance head. LOAD ORDER for the new sheets: 38, 39, 40, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 47, 48 and 65, 66 are configuration and must be loaded before 12_Employees. Everything from 46 and 49 upward is transaction or output data and loads after 37.
